APCTT-C01.quote: This third component of EGRET involves applying the Weighted Regressions on Time, Discharge, and Season (WRTDS) smoothing method (Hirsch and others, 2010) to interpret the behavior of the water-quality analyte of interest
APCTT-C01.note: Statistical basis (WRTDS, lowess smoothing on p26) with citations.

APCTT-C02.quote: The body of this report serves as a user guide to the EGRET R package, providing detailed guidance on installation and use of the software, documentation of the analysis methods used, as well as guidance on some of the kinds of questions and approaches that the software can facilitate.
APCTT-C02.note: Application: retrieval and trend analysis of river data.

APCTT-C03.quote: Figure 1 is an image of the report provided in the Choptank nitrate example.
APCTT-C03.note: Worked example outputs show the packages' key functions; WRTDS surface estimation described with results (p56).

APCTT-C04.note: No testing of the software is reported.

APCTT-C05.note: No validation of results against independent data is reported in this guide.

APCTT-C06.quote: In the examples to follow, we consider a streamgage (Choptank River near Greensboro, Maryland) with USGS site ID 01491000, and we look for daily mean discharge and sample values of dissolved nitrate plus nitrite, which has parameter code 00631.
APCTT-C06.note: The software demonstrated on real monitoring records (Choptank, Colorado River at Lees Ferry, Vermilion River).

APCTT-C07.note: Distributed as R packages, but the report does not state operational use by its users.

APCTT-C11.quote: The grid spacing is 0.0625 years (1/16th of a year), so in this case, the time values for the grid would total 497 values (16 per year times 13 years plus one additional grid for the end of the last year).

APCTT-C12.quote: This report is a guide to a tightly coupled system of software for doing both the data retrieval and the data analysis.
APCTT-C12.note: Evidence concerns the EGRET and dataRetrieval packages.
